messages.text: I’ll read the full spec and each file in its `context:` list before making changes, then verify the requested behavior.

The spec requires fresh authorization inside the write transaction and validation of the reason before handling a repeat cancellation. I’ll use the existing transaction and DTO helpers, and add a separate admin command.

The existing member-cancellation code already preserves the first cancellation’s metadata and handles transaction rollback. I’m adding the admin command and the cancellation form next, then testing expiry, role changes, repeat requests, and failures before and after audit insertion.

The first focused run passed the cancellation, boundary, identity, and rollback checks. One test fixture needs correcting: form requests use a hidden CSRF field, so its JSON-style header caused a 403 before the intended format check. I’ll correct that fixture and continue with the browser and concurrency checks.

The JavaScript checks pass, including confirmation, disabled controls, retained input, malformed responses, manual retries, and failed refreshes after a successful cancellation. The full regression suites and 20-round HTTP race test are running. I’ll now exercise the page at desktop and phone sizes.

The regression suites passed: 167 Python tests and 228 JavaScript tests, with no skips. All 20 HTTP race rounds also passed: both callers received the same result, and each round stored exactly one cancellation audit. Faults before audit insertion, after insertion, and at COMMIT each rolled back the booking, slots, and audit.

The browser checks passed at both sizes, including reason visibility to the member, manual retry after a dropped response, and session loss. Visual inspection found an oversized checkbox and collapsed line breaks in the new form. I’ve adjusted the styling and will rerun the browser checks to capture the final layout.

The final browser runs passed, and I inspected the desktop and phone screenshots. The form is readable, long text wraps, and neither layout overflows horizontally. I’m recording the final evidence paths and known limits for the initial implementation handoff.

Implemented Story 2.5 in X: independent admin cancellation service, protected API, reason/confirmation UI, and acceptance tests.

- Python: **167 passed**, no skips.
- JavaScript: **228 passed**, no skips.
- HTTP: **20 races passed**, identical responses and one cancellation audit per round; audit and COMMIT fault rollback verified.
- Browser: **1280×800 and 390×844 passed**; screenshots inspected, member-visible reasons verified.

Full changes, commands, evidence, and limitations: [implementation report](/Users/mima0000/Documents/Codex/2026-11-12/bmad-b/work/experiment-a-run-20261112/X/work/admin-cancel-implementation-report.json).

No in-scope work remains; independent review awaits the parent snapshot. Browser controls reject unsafe JavaScript integer IDs; API supports positive signed 64-bit IDs.
